subject: Tailwind (HelioLabs) — node staging verification and soft-lock proposal
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tailwind (HelioLabs) — node staging verification and soft-lock proposal

Team,

We are in late-stage with HelioLabs (deal TW-2029-1123). They sign next week in principle, but procurement needs an internal capacity confirmation to move to commercial. Key ask: can we provision 8 H100-80GB production nodes + 4 warm standby nodes (same HW profile) starting 2029-08-15 for the initial rollout window (30 days) with an option to scale to 16 prod nodes by month two?

Traffic profile: sustained 3–5 qps bursty peaks to 10 qps for evaluation jobs. Model: quantized 70B LLM variants (they've asked for H100 pref but will accept A100 fallback with profiling). SLA target: p95 generation latency < 800ms.

Please run an availability check across the US pool and flag conflicts with any near-term reservations. If H100s are scarce, propose a fallback mapping (A100 mapping + pre-warm caches) and indicate the cost delta. If we can, propose a soft-lock window we can present to the customer (dates and node count) so procurement can tie action to the mutual action plan.

I've attached the current capacity MOP and the HelioLabs summary. Need an ops snapshot by EOD so I can share an external ask to Ravi.

Thanks,

Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: tailwind_capacity_mop_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet — summary of node profile & baseline throughput)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jul 2029 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tailwind (HelioLabs) — node staging verification and soft-lock proposal

Lauren —

Quick inventory snapshot beneath; full CSV attached. Short answer: H100-80GB capacity in the US pool is tight the week of 8/12–8/20 due to two scheduled migrations and a committed internal POC. We can support the requested baseline with a conditional soft-hold, but some tradeoffs:

- Current free H100-80GB nodes (US pool): 10 nodes available during 8/10–9/30 window.
- Standing holds / near-term commitments: 6 nodes are already earmarked (migrations/POCs) — some are convertible.
- Proposal: soft-lock 12 nodes (8 prod + 4 warm) from 2029-08-10 to 2029-09-30. If H100 supply becomes constrained we can automatically fall back to A100-40GB with the following plan:
  - Fallback mapping: 1 H100 -> 1.6 A100 (pre-quantization + perf tuning)
  - Expected p95 latency change: +150–220ms for the same model unless we adjust batch sizing and KV caching.
  - Cost delta: ~+18% token cost on A100 fallback (estimate).

Operational notes / blockers:
- We have a concurrent late-stage request for H100 on 8/15 (internal reserved deal). If we grant a soft-lock to HelioLabs now, we should mark the reservation as timeboxed (auto-release 08/25 if not signed) to avoid deadlocks.
- We can prepare a temporary pre-warm of KV caches for HelioLabs on 8/13 (one-time ops cost).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Approve soft-lock dates (8/10–9/30) with auto-release clause (08/25) to offer to customer.
2) If approved, ops will place the soft-hold and publish inventory_snapshot_20290730.csv to the drive.
3) Align finance for preliminary price uplift if we must route to A100.

I'll place the inventory snapshot in Drive and share the link once the soft-lock is approved.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: inventory_snapshot_20290730.csv (node-level inventory export)

Cc: HelioLabs Procurement <procurement@heliolabs.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jul 2029 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Tailwind — preliminary capacity proposal and mutual action plan (please review)

Ravi —

Thanks again for the intake call this morning. Per the internal availability check, we can provision the 8 H100-80GB prod nodes + 4 warm standby nodes you requested, subject to a near-term soft-lock and final signatures. Karthik proposed the following customer-facing plan:

- Soft-lock 12 nodes (8 prod + 4 warm) from 2029-08-10 to 2029-09-30 with auto-release 2029-08-25 if the contract is not executed.
- If H100 supply becomes constrained, we will automatically enable an A100 fallback and run a short profiling window (1–2 days) to tune batch sizes and caching; we will disclose the perf/cost delta.
- Target production start (traffic ramp): 2029-08-15.

Attached is a draft mutual action plan (MAP) outlining signoffs, SOC2 evidence checklist, and procurement milestones. Can you confirm a target sign-off date for the MAP (we're asking for 2029-08-06 so ops can place the soft-lock)? If procurement needs more time we can shift the auto-release window, but need a firm date to avoid over-committing fleet to multiple late-stage opportunities.

If you approve, we'll place the soft-lock today and share the inventory snapshot + costs for final review.

Best,

Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Attachments: mutual_action_plan-tailwind.pdf (MAP draft, includes proposed soft-lock dates and SOC2 checklist)
From: Ravi Iyer <ravi@heliolabs.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: HelioLabs Procurement <procurement@heliolabs.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Jul 2029 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tailwind — preliminary capacity proposal and mutual action plan (please review)

Hi Lauren,

Thanks — appreciate the proactive coordination. Procurement is reviewing the MAP now. Two quick items from our side:

1) SOC2 evidence: procurement needs the attestation and the last 12-month audit report. Can you include the SOC2 summary in the MAP or point us to the portal where we can download it?

2) We can tentatively agree to the 2029-08-06 MAP sign-off target, but procurement wants the soft-lock extended to auto-release on 2029-08-28 (they may need an extra week for internal approvals). Will that work?

If you can confirm the SOC2 delivery method and the slight extension to 08/28 for auto-release, we'll move forward with internal approvals and aim to execute the agreement by 2029-08-12.

Ravi Iyer
Head of Platform, HelioLabs
ravi@heliolabs.com
